messages:
slo-bot: ALERT p99 latency breach on /v1/streaming (us-east-1) — p95 320ms, p99 1.9s, streaming stalls detected

nora (oncall): paging now, taking lead. Investigating KV cache metrics and eviction rates. @raj can you grab shard telemetry?

raj: on it. pulling kv slab and eviction histograms. initial read shows prefill bytes spiking ~00:13 UTC, slab occupancy 94% on shard-7

nora (oncall): re-route policy triggered fallback to model-smaller in one AZ. Are customers seeing errors or just slow streaming?

ops-bot: Customer-impact: 32 sessions with visible stalls, 6 session timeouts >30s, no 5xxs reported yet

eli: looks like prefill vs decode imbalance — many requests hitting prefill path creating large KV entries, while decode threads starved. p99 correlates with eviction churn.

sara: logs show repeated eviction thrash: "evict_item cache_miss prefetch_fail" across worker-7/12. Also seeing GC spikes in decoder JVM (if applicable) — but primary looks cache.

incident-bot: INCIDENT created INC-202503-114 by nora — severity P1. Pager duty runbook: kv-prefill-eviction

nora (oncall): immediate mitigations: 1) reduce prefill size threshold on route /v1/streaming to 512 tokens 2) increase decode concurrency on affected hosts 3) temporarily increase soft eviction margin to free slabs. Which is fastest to apply?

raj: I can flip soft eviction margin and prefill threshold via config flag; patch will roll to shard-7 / shard-8 only. decode concurrency change requires deploy (longer)

maya (devex): heads up — turning prefill threshold down could reduce quality for long-context customers. We should notify SRE and product of possible regressions.

eli: execute plan: raj apply config toggle (soft-evict + prefill-threshold) to 0.7/512, track streaming p95/p99. I'll watch decoder threadpool.

raj: applied: set kv.prefill_threshold_tokens=512, kv.soft_evict_margin=0.7 on shard-7,8 — rolling restart avoided (hot-config)

nora (oncall): monitoring — graphs: p95 dropped from 320ms -> 210ms over 30s, p99 1.9s -> 480ms and falling

ops-bot: NOTE: some sessions report shorter completions; 2 customers (acct-332, acct-981) flagged quality drop on long prompts

sara: logged a mitigation note in INC-202503-114 with commands and flags. Suggest follow-up: analyze prefill usage patterns, tighten per-route quotas.

eli: next steps: 1) schedule a canary rollout of improved eviction algorithm that prioritizes prefill TTLs 2) run offline eval for quality impact of reduced prefill

nora (oncall): handing off to raj for overnight watch. @sara will own customer comms; @maya prepare note for customers with long-context workloads. I'll remain available for escalation.

raj: handover ack. I'll keep watch and escalate if p99 > 1s or error rate >0.1%

maya (devex): drafting customer advisory: short note explaining transient latency, steps taken, potential quality impact and expected ETA for full fix ~24-48h

incident-bot: UPDATE INC-202503-114 state=mitigated by nora at 5050002245 — p99 normalized to 420ms; continue monitoring

nora (oncall): closing notes: root cause hypothesis: KV cache fragmentation + prefill-heavy burst causing eviction churn and decode starvation -> streaming tail stalls. Mitigations: soft-evict margin change + prefill threshold reduction stabilized tail. Follow-ups: long-term fix (eviction algorithm + per-route prefill caps + cache compaction) + postmortem in 24h.

raj: adding relevant logs to ticket: /var/log/kv/shard-7/evict-2025-03-11.log

sara: notified account owners via email; listed affected request ids in the incident ticket.

ops-bot: Reaction: :thumbsup: from 5 users

nora (oncall): thanks team — great triage. I'll open a postmortem draft and assign owners.
